translationRepairs: Andou received the staff of authority, became Palace Attendant among the Scattered Cavalry, took command of Xu and five other provinces plus Liang in Yu, was named General Who Guards the South and Xu governor, and was created Duke of Hedong.

Andou received the staff of authority, became Palace Attendant among the Scattered Cavalry, took command of military affairs in the five provinces of Xu, Southern Yan, Northern Yan, Qing, and Ji, plus Liang Commandery in Yu, was named Grand General Who Guards the South and Xu governor, and was created Duke of Hedong.
都督徐、南、北兗、青、冀五州、豫州之梁郡諸軍事 lists five provinces including Xu (Xu, Southern Yan, Northern Yan, Qing, Ji), not Xu plus five others; 鎮南大將軍 is Grand General.
He rose to secretariat attendant and chief rectifier for Hedong.
He rose to Attendant Gentleman on the staff of the Minister over the Masses and chief rectifier for Hedong.
司徒從事中郎 is an attendant gentleman on the staff of the Minister over the Masses (司徒), not a secretariat attendant.
Posthumously he was made General Who Conquers the West and Yong governor; his son kept the title.
Posthumously he was made General Who Conquers the West and Yong governor; his viscountcy remained as before.
子如故 means his viscount rank (平溫子, s0050) was unchanged; it does not refer to a son.
When Cao Huzhi of Yong feigned surrender to Xiao Ze, Zhendu was ordered to lead four generals from Xiangyang and came back empty-handed.
When Cao Hu, Xiao Ze's governor of Yong, feigned surrender, Zhendu was ordered to lead four generals out from Xiangyang and came back empty-handed.
The name is 曹虎 (之 is a particle), and he was Xiao Ze's own governor feigning surrender to Wei, not feigning surrender to Xiao Ze.
He rose from Grand Temple aide to General Who Conquers the Barbarians and Scattered-Cavalry Grandee, then Left General and Palace Grand Master.
He rose from Assistant to the Chamberlain for Ceremonials to General Who Conquers the Barbarians and Grand Master of Palace Leisure, then Left General and Palace Grand Master.
太常丞 is assistant to the Chamberlain for Ceremonials and 中散大夫 is Grand Master of Palace Leisure; neither involves the Grand Temple or the Scattered Cavalry.
Huaiji, a concubine's eldest son, overstay mourning and gave the emperor a dozen of his father's girls and their instruments.
Huaiji, eldest son by a concubine, after more than a year of mourning presented over ten of his father's entertainers with their instruments, and Emperor Shizong accepted them.
Fixes ungrammatical "overstay"; 居喪過周 means after mourning had passed a full year, and 世宗納焉 (Shizong accepted them) was omitted.
Xiao Yan sent a host to raid Xu and Yan; Xing Luan of Andong campaigned against them, and an edict made Huaiji army secretary to Luan in his present rank.
Xiao Yan sent a host to raid Xu and Yan; General Who Calms the East Xing Luan campaigned against them, and an edict made Huaiji army secretary to Luan in his present rank.
安東 is the office General Who Calms the East (安東將軍) held by Xing Luan, not a place called Andong.
Yu city's people killed their governor for Xiao Yan; Qi Gouren held Xuancheng, and south of it only Yiyang still stood.

At that time Bai Zaosheng, a townsman of the Yu provincial city, killed the governor and handed Xuanhu to Xiao Yan; Yan's general Qi Gouren held the city, so from Xuanhu south to Anlu only Yiyang still stood.
The idiomatic text omits the named rebel 白早生 (Bai Zaosheng) and renders 懸瓠 (Xuanhu) as Xuancheng; it also drops Anlu (安陸).
In Yan chang he became Liang governor at the same rank.
In Yanchang he became Liang governor at the same rank.
The reign name 延昌 is Yanchang; "Yan chang" is a corrupted split word.

Empress Dowager Wensheng and Emperor Gaozu received him in the Hall of Imperial Trust, bestowing wine and food, one carriage, three horses, and two hundred bolts of silk, and sent him off with honors.
Empress Dowager Wenming and Emperor Gaozu received him in the Hall of Imperial Trust, bestowing wine and food, one carriage, three horses, and two hundred bolts of silk, and sent him off with honors.
The source title is 文明太后 (Empress Dowager Wenming), not Wensheng.
his imperial grant wife Yuan bore Zurong and Zuhui.
his wife granted by the throne, Lady Yuan, bore two sons, Zurong and Zuhui.
"his imperial grant wife Yuan" is ungrammatical; 賜妻元氏生二子 = the wife of the Yuan clan granted to him bore two sons.
At Shen gui's end he became Bearer of the Staff and Eastern Yu governor.
At the end of Shengui he became Bearer of the Staff and Eastern Yu governor.
The reign name 神龜 is Shengui; "Shen gui" is a corrupted split word.
Back at court he was Forward General, Grand Minister chief clerk, and northern commissioner.
Back at court he was Forward General, Chief Clerk to the Grand Commandant, and concurrently Northern Route Branch Secretariat Commissioner.
太尉長史 is chief clerk to the Grand Commandant (太尉), not a "Grand Minister"; 兼尚書北道行臺 is a concurrent branch-secretariat commission.
He served secretariat, Yan, rectifier, Central Army general, and Direct Scattered-Cavalry Attendant.
He passed through Secretariat aide, vice minister, Yan governor, grand rectifier, General of the Central Army, and Direct Attendant in the Scattered Cavalry.
The idiomatic list is garbled ("served secretariat, Yan, rectifier"), dropping that he was Yan governor (兗州刺史) and vice minister (侍郎).
Early in Shen gui he became General Who Raises the Fierce and Dongping governor.
Early in Shengui he became General Who Raises the Fierce and Dongping governor.
The reign name 神龜 is Shengui; "Shen gui" is a corrupted split word.
Early in Shen gui he was Right General and Bin governor.
Early in Shengui he was Right General and Bin governor.
The reign name 神龜 is Shengui; "Shen gui" is a corrupted split word.
In Zhenguang year five Bin rose, Long rebels joined, and besieged the city.
In Zhengguang year five Bin rose, Long rebels joined, and besieged the city.
The reign name 正光 is Zhengguang, not "Zhenguang".
Early in Yan chang he took Qinghe, resigned ill, and returned to dragon-agile and scattered-cavalry ranks.
Early in Yanchang he took Qinghe, resigned ill, and returned to dragon-agile and scattered-cavalry ranks.
The reign name 延昌 is Yanchang; "Yan chang" is a corrupted split word.
Early in Zhenguang Prince Xi of Zhongshan rebelled against Yuan Cha; Wenwei killed his envoy and resisted.
Early in Zhengguang Prince Xi of Zhongshan rebelled against Yuan Cha; Wenwei killed his envoy and resisted.
The reign name 正光 is Zhengguang, not "Zhenguang".
Liu Yu's brother Wenbing turned him back; Yu restored his rank.
Liu Yu sent Wenxiu's younger brother Wenbing to win him back; Wenxiu returned to Yu, who restored his rank.
The idiomatic line makes Wenbing Liu Yu's brother; 文秀弟文炳 is Wenxiu's younger brother, sent by Liu Yu.
Nephew Anshi surrendered with Xiahou Daogian in Zhengshi.
Nephew Anshi surrendered with Xiahou Daoqian in Zhengshi.
The name 夏侯道遷 is Xiahou Daoqian; "Daogian" is a misspelling.
Huang Tiansi built at Chiting and posted Huang Gongshang at Chong.
Xiao Yan's Jianning administrator Huang Tianci built a fort at Chiting and again sent his general Huang Gongshang to camp at Chong city, holding out against Changfeng.
黃天賜 is romanized Huang Tianci (賜 = ci), and the idiomatic rendering drops his office and master and the standoff with Changfeng.
Eight feet tall, fierce and fruit-bearing with military strategy, his appearance and bearing quite unlike ordinary barbarians.
Eight feet tall, bold and resolute with military strategy, his appearance and bearing quite unlike ordinary barbarians.
雄果 means bold and resolute; "fierce and fruit-bearing" mistranslates 果 as fruit.
When Bai Zaosheng rebelled in Yuzhou, an edict to Yizong said: "Xuancheng is an important border stronghold, close to Song and Ying; the weight of the southern frontier entrusted to it is not light.
When Bai Zaosheng rebelled in Yuzhou, an edict to Yizong said: "Xuanhu is an important border stronghold, close to Song and Ying; the weight of the southern frontier entrusted to it is not light.
The stronghold 懸瓠 is Xuanhu, not "Xuancheng".

Yan garrison commander Zhao Wenju led a host to resist; Lusheng broke them, capturing Wenju and the lieutenants Hu Jianxing, Gu Hao, Zhuang Yuanchong and others, beheading more than five thousand, drowning fifteen hundred, grain boats burned clean.

Xiao Yan's garrison commander Zhao Wenju led a host to resist; Lusheng broke them, capturing Wenju and the lieutenants Hu Jianxing, Gu Hao, Zhuang Yuanchong and others, beheading more than five thousand, drowning fifteen hundred, grain boats burned clean.
衍戍主 is Xiao Yan's (衍) garrison commander; "Yan garrison commander" misreads the ruler's name as a place.
Jingyao was chained to the place of the imperial progress and several times beheaded.
Jingyao was sent in chains to the place of the imperial progress, where his crimes were enumerated and he was beheaded.
數而斬之 means "enumerated (his crimes) and beheaded him", not "several times beheaded".
He served the south as southern conqueror, Jiang governor, and Fengcheng baron.
He served the south as Grand General Who Guards the South, Jiang governor, and Founding Duke of Fengcheng.
豐城縣開國公 is a dukedom (公), not a barony; 鎮南大將軍 is the Grand General Who Guards the South.
In the third year of Jingming, Bozhi sent envoys with a secret memorial requesting surrender and sent his son the champion general, Xu governor, and Baron of Yongchang Huya as hostage.
In the third year of Jingming, Bozhi sent envoys with a secret memorial requesting surrender and sent his son the champion general, Xu governor, and Marquis of Yongchang Huya as hostage.
永昌縣開國侯 is a marquisate (侯), not a barony.
Second summer he became Grand Master; Huya Forward General.
In the second year, in summer, he became Grand Master of Splendid Happiness; Huya became Forward General.
二年夏 is "summer of the second year" (of Zhengshi), not a "second summer".

Biao later observed Shuzhen's words and color and greatly suspected something odd; on pushing investigation it was that he was Shuye's nephew by a sister, sent by Shuye, plotting as inside agent—the wife and children carried were also false.

Biao later observed Shuzhen's words and color and greatly suspected something odd; on pushing investigation it was that he was the son of Shuye's paternal aunt, sent by Shuye, plotting as inside agent—the wife and children carried were also false.
姑兒 is the son of a paternal aunt (a cousin), not a "nephew by a sister".
He died in Yan chang year four at eighty-one.
He died in Yanchang year four at eighty-one.
The reign name 延昌 is Yanchang; "Yan chang" is a corrupted split word.
Zhongjing's surrender brought glory; Bi and allies shared rank.
Zhongjing offered his land and allegiance, bringing glory to the court; his kinsmen all held rank.
The idiomatic "Bi and allies shared rank" is a garbled gloss of 人位並列; there is no "Bi" in the source here.
Puban in Hedong was the Xue homeland.

The seat of Taizhou was Puban in Hedong, the home province of the Xue clan; at the time it was an honor to serve as governor of one's home province, so many grandfathers and grandsons held this office.
The idiomatic rendering drops the Taizhou identification and the reason the Xue held the post.
At the beginning of Jingming Xiao Yan sent army commander Wu Ziyang leading troops to raid the Three Passes: according to juan 8, Basic Annals of Emperor Shizong, Jingming year one
The idiomatic rendering omits the lemma naming Xiao Yan and Wu Ziyang and the juan citation.
Xiao Yan rebelled eleventh month that year.
Only in the eleventh month of that year did Xiao Yan raise troops against Baojuan.
The idiomatic rendering omits Baojuan, the target of Xiao Yan's rising, which is the point of the note.
